content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: switch on IVR callback on both queues 18:00–20:00 at no extra cost; the disruption window is predicted at 95.5% against an 80% target.","why":"The general queue is running 44% over forecast (2,409 calls vs 1,669) because of the 09:00 pre-approved loan email (MKT-2026-551). Loan and new-offer enquiries are 3–4x normal, and service level has dipped as low as 24% today. For 14:45–18:45 the model predicts the target is met even with no action (P0 at 95.3%). P1 adds evening callbacks for free, giving 95.5% overall, 92.9% on general and 98.0% on payments, with a 0.8% abandon rate. P1 follows policy, so it is the cheapest compliant plan.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) also costs nothing and predicts 95.3%. P1 gives slightly better window figures (95.5%, 0.8% abandon vs 0.9%) and puts evening callback cover in place at no cost. General is predicted fractionally lower under P1 (92.9% vs 93.4%), while payments improves (98.0% vs 97.1%).","P2 (₹144) and P3 (₹528) predict higher results (97.0% and 97.8%; rest of day 92.7% and 94.5%). Both break policy CX-01, because they would play a known-issue message when there is no confirmed outage or incident. A marketing campaign does not count.","P4 (chat deflection, ₹552) follows policy and predicts 96.3% (general 94.0%, rest of day 93.0%). It costs ₹552 for a target that P1 already meets for free.","With P1, rest of day stays at 89.6%, the same as doing nothing. The paid options lift it to 92.7–94.5%."],"watch":"The forecast predicts 95.3% even with no action, yet general has run 35–74% over forecast in every interval since 12:45 and dipped as low as 24%. Check that the predictions reflect the campaign volume. If general calls keep running well above forecast or service level stays low, P4 is the compliant step up. No escalation is needed."}
